root_idea.summary: The root centers on becoming free from admixture and thereby clear, pure, or distinct.
root_idea.development: The semantic development runs from milk becoming clear of froth or biestings to clear, correct, and intelligible Arabic or speech, and further to things becoming manifest. The festival term الفِصْح is treated separately as a lexical branch not belonging to this core development.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Displayed as the Quran-attested comparative adjective أَفْصَحُ, normalized from the QAC nominal morphology identity.

senses.definition: More eloquent, clearer, or more articulate in speech.
senses.usage_conditions: A comparative adjective used in أَفْصَحُ مِنِّي لِسَانًا, comparing the clarity and eloquence of Aaron’s speech with Moses’ speech.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become clear and free from admixture; especially, for milk, to lose its froth or become clear of its biestings.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Also used of a thing becoming clear of what was mixed with it.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become good, correct, clear, intelligible, or eloquent in language; for a foreigner, to become able to speak Arabic intelligibly.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Said of a person’s language, dialect, or speech; the evidence also records its use for an Arab becoming more eloquent.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become apparent or to come suddenly upon someone, said of daybreak.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Occurs in the expression قَدْ فَصَحَكَ الصُّبْحُ and in the reported variant فَصَحَهُ الصُّبْحُ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To make a foreigner’s tongue speak Arabic.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A causative use referring to bringing someone to Arabic speech.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become clear or free from turbidity or admixture.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Said of urine becoming clear and of the milk of a ewe, she-goat, or she-camel becoming free from froth or biestings.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To speak clearly, correctly, intelligibly, or eloquently; also, to speak Arabic.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used absolutely or with speech and language expressions; it can also describe an animal uttering a sound or cry clearly.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To explain something or disclose and reveal one’s meaning.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used with عَنْ, as in explaining a matter or revealing an intention.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become clearly apparent, manifest, or evident.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Said of daybreak and, more generally, of a thing becoming evident.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To get clear of or escape from something.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used with مِنْ; the cited applications include getting clear of winter or another difficult condition.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To enter upon or celebrate the festival called الفِصْح, Easter.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used in the plural أَفْصَحُوا for Christians, with the festival involving the ending of a fast and eating meat.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To affect, display, or make use of eloquence in speech.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: May imply adopting the appearance or manner of those known for eloquence.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To judge a word or phrase to be eloquent, chaste, or free from barbarousness.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The extension to judging a person eloquent is reported more tentatively and may be post-classical.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To ask or desire someone to explain something.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used with عَنْ in the cited construction اِسْتَفْصَحْتُهُ عَنْ كَذَا.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A cloudless day.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The reported explanations differ as to whether the absence of clouds is associated with cold or with its absence.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The Christian festival of Easter; also, the Jewish Passover.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Also called عِيدُ الفِصْح; the Christian observance is described as following a period of fasting.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Milk that has become clear of froth or biestings, including milk that comes after the biestings cease.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A lexical adjective applied to purified milk.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Chaste, correct, clear, or eloquent in language; applied to a word, expression, language, tongue, speaker, or writer.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The quality involves freedom from linguistic strangeness or incongruity and, for speech, clarity and freedom from impediment; it may also describe a clear animal cry.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A speaking human being, in contrast with an animal lacking the faculty of speech.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Occurs in the contrast فَصِيحٌ وَصَامِتٌ, where the former denotes human property and the latter animal property.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Chasteness, correctness, clarity, or eloquence of a word, language, or speaker.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: For words it denotes freedom from strangeness and incongruous combination; for language, freedom from weakness of construction; for a speaker, the faculty of expressing what is intended clearly.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The quality of being more or most chaste, clear, or eloquent in language.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An abstract noun formed from the comparative or superlative adjective أَفْصَحُ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A place where the festival of Easter is celebrated.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The term may also refer to a place where the Passover is celebrated.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Anything clearly apparent, manifest, or evident.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An active-participial adjective used substantivally.

cautions: The QAC occurrence is tagged as nominal, while أَفْصَحُ is presented here as the comparative adjective identified by its Quranic construction and lexical evidence.
الفِصْح, the festival term, is listed under the same orthographic root in the lexical evidence but is treated as a separate branch from the root’s core purity-and-clarity development.
